title: Azoth unit vocabulary
description: The canonical units a spec may declare, each with the dimension it carries and the name it has in `uom` and in `pint`. This is the one hand-written source for that list; `tools/gen_vocabulary.py` compiles it into Rust, Python and JSON Schema, and `--check` fails if any of the three has drifted. **No magnitude appears in it.** A conversion factor is a number the units libraries already know, and restating one here would be a second answer to a question they have answered - the failure that produced this repository's millimetre defect. `additionalProperties: false` throughout, so a field cannot be added without a deliberate edit here.

schema_version.description: Bump only if the format changes; the generator refuses a version it does not know rather than guessing at what a newer shape meant.

slots.description: The base dimensions, in the order every exponent tuple below is written in. The order is uom::si::ISQ's, and it is not cosmetic: the generated exponent tuples and the generated uom quantity types are both built from it, so a different order permutes all of them at once.

dimensions.description: Every dimension a unit below carries, named once. A unit refers to one by id, so two units that share a dimension cannot be given different exponents by accident.

dimension_id.description: A dimension's name, unique within `dimensions`. The generator refuses a duplicate rather than letting the last one win.

exponents.description: One exponent per slot, in the order `slots` declares. The bound is well inside the i8 the generated Rust carries, so a value that would overflow is refused here rather than at codegen.

uom_path.description: Where uom carries this dimension, as `<dimension module>::<unit>` - the path `.new::<..>()` takes. The quantity type is not part of it: the generator derives that from the exponents, so a wrong exponent fails to compile instead of being waved through by a matching name. The module is checked against the dimension's own quantity, because uom's module for a quantity is its name in snake case.

id.description: The canonical unit string, exactly as a spec spells it in `unit:`. This is the string that reaches a user, so it is the one entry in the table that is a readable unit rather than an identifier.

pint.description: The unit's name in pint's registry. pint supplies the conversion factor, which is why none is written down.

uom.description: Where uom carries this dimension. Absent where uom has no such quantity: uom's `quantity!` macro must run inside `uom::si`, and the `Units` trait that makes `.new::<u>()` compile is assembled by `system!` from a closed list, so no crate outside uom can add a quantity to it. A unit with no `uom` converts by the identity, because it is already its own SI base unit.

rust_ctor.description: The hand-written constructor in crates/azoth-core/src/units.rs that the generated conversion calls. The generator never invents one, so a unit that claims a uom path and names no constructor is refused.
